65	  private
66	    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
67	    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
68	
69	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]            using ( _≈_ )
70	                                renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
71	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
72	  open Group-Op 𝒢               using  ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong
73	                                       ; assoc-law ; invˡ-law )
74	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ  using  ( ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙
75	                                       ; \\-leftDividesˡ ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
76	  open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup  using  ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed ; ⁻¹-closed )
77	
78	  infix 4 _∼_
79	
80	  -- x and y lie in the same left coset of H when x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H.
81	  _∼_ : G → G → Type ℓ
82	  x ∼ y = x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ H
83	```
84	
85	#### `_∼_` is an equivalence relation
86	
87	+  Reflexivity is `ε ∈ H` transported along `x ⁻¹ ∙ x ≈ ε`.
88	+  Symmetry is closure of `H` under inverses, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x`.
89	+  Transitivity is closure under products, since `(x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z`.
90	
91	```agda
92	  ∼-refl : ∀ {x} → x ∼ x
93	  ∼-refl {x} = respects (≈sym (invˡ-law x)) ε-closed
94	
95	  ∼-sym : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → y ∼ x
96	  ∼-sym {x} {y} x∼y = respects inv-eq (⁻¹-closed x∼y)
97	    where
98	    inv-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ x
99	    inv-eq = begin
100	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ (x ⁻¹) y ⟩
101	      y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-involutive x) ⟩
102	      y ⁻¹ ∙ x          ∎
103	
104	  ∼-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x ∼ y → y ∼ z → x ∼ z
105	  ∼-trans {x} {y} {z} x∼y y∼z = respects prod-eq (∙-closed x∼y y∼z)
106	    where
107	    prod-eq : (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ z
108	    prod-eq = begin
109	      (x ⁻¹ ∙ y) ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z)  ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) y (y ⁻¹ ∙ z) ⟩
110	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (y ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ z))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesˡ y z) ⟩
111	      x ⁻¹ ∙ z                 ∎
112	
113	  ∼-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _∼_
114	  ∼-isEquivalence = record { refl = ∼-refl ; sym = ∼-sym ; trans = ∼-trans }
115	
116	  ∼-equivalence : Equivalence G {ℓ}
117	  ∼-equivalence = _∼_ , ∼-isEquivalence
118	```
119	
120	#### Compatibility lemmas
121	
122	Two facts are needed before the coset relation can be used as an equality.
123	
124	`≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} says the group's own setoid equality refines the coset
125	relation, which is what makes the quotient map well defined: equal elements land
126	in the same coset.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} says left translation by any group
127	element preserves the coset relation, which is what lets `g ∙_` descend to the
128	coset space.
129	
130	Both are proved the same way, by supplying `respects`{.AgdaFunction} with an
131	equality between the relevant `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` witnesses: for `≈⇒∼`{.AgdaFunction} that
132	witness reduces to `ε` and membership follows from `ε-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, and for
133	`∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} the `g` cancels, so the translated witness equals the
134	original.  `∼-congˡ`{.AgdaFunction} is what
135	[Classical.Structures.Group.GSet][] uses to build the coset algebra.
136	
137	```agda
138	  -- The setoid equality refines the coset equality (the quotient map is well defined).
139	  ≈⇒∼ : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∼ y
140	  ≈⇒∼ {x} {y} x≈y = respects (≈sym unit-eq) ε-closed
141	    where
142	    unit-eq : x ⁻¹ ∙ y ≈ ε
143	    unit-eq = ≈trans (∙-cong (⁻¹-cong x≈y) ≈refl) (invˡ-law y)
144	
145	  -- Left translation by any group element preserves the coset equality.
146	  ∼-congˡ : ∀ g {x y} → x ∼ y → (g ∙ x) ∼ (g ∙ y)
147	  ∼-congˡ g {x} {y} x∼y = respects (≈sym transl-eq) x∼y
148	    where
149	    transl-eq : (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y) ≈ x ⁻¹ ∙ y
150	    transl-eq = begin
151	      (g ∙ x) ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)     ≈⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ g x) ≈refl ⟩
152	      x ⁻¹ ∙ g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y)    ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ⁻¹) (g ⁻¹) (g ∙ y) ⟩
153	      x ⁻¹ ∙ (g ⁻¹ ∙ (g ∙ y))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ g y) ⟩
154	      x ⁻¹ ∙ y                 ∎
155	```
156	
157	#### Decidability
158	
159	The coset relation is decidable exactly when membership in `H`{.AgdaBound} is:
160	whether `x ∼ y` is, definitionally, whether the single product `x ⁻¹ ∙ y` lies in
161	`H`{.AgdaBound}.[^1]
162	
163	```agda
164	  -- With decidable membership in H, the coset relation is decidable.
165	  ∼-dec : (∀ x → Dec (x ∈ H)) → ∀ x y → Dec (x ∼ y)
166	  ∼-dec H-dec x y = H-dec (x ⁻¹ ∙ y)
167	```
168	
169	#### The quotient setoid `G/H`
170	
171	The coset space is the carrier of `𝒢` under the coset equality, assembled by the
172	quotient construction of [Setoid.Relations.Quotients][].
173	
174	```agda
175	  cosetSetoid : Setoid α ℓ
176	  cosetSetoid = G / ∼-equivalence
177	```
178	
179	---
180	
181	[^1]:  This is the Layer-D decision procedure that sits beside the semantic
182	       relation, per the two-layer discipline ([ADR-008]; audit A2 of
183	       `docs/notes/flrp-wp7-audits.md`).
